content.text:
TiNbO4 (mp-1216686) is the only phase I can identify. It matches the peak pattern, but the fit is poor in absolute terms (R-factor 0.84), so treat this as a best match rather than a confirmed one.

- **Pattern match:** TiNbO4's simulated peaks are at about 18.5°, a doublet at 26.4° and 27.35°, a main peak near 35.3°, and further peaks near 39°, 41°, 54–57° and 69°. The observed pattern has all of these, at 18.25°, 26.65° and 27.65°, about 35.3°, and so on.
- **Why the fit is poor:** the observed peaks are shifted from the simulation, but not all in one direction. The 18.25° peak sits lower than simulated, while the doublet sits higher. The fit tool only allows one uniform stretch of the whole cell, so it cannot follow this; it settled at +1.5%. The leftovers have the up-and-down shape of misplaced peaks rather than new peaks. That points to the real cell being distorted a bit differently from this structure, not to a second phase.
- **Other candidates:** a three-way fit of NaSmO2, Eu3AlO5 and KNaSmTaO5 explained almost none of the observed peaks (R = 0.96). Adding Li4TiV3O8 to TiNbO4 barely changed the fit (R 0.84 to 0.84). I did not run HoNiO3, Ca2TiCrO6, Sr4Fe2CoNiO12 or NaPr2RuO6. I set them aside because these perovskite-type structures should have their strongest peak near 32°, and the observed pattern has none there. That reasoning is mine, not a tool result.
